header.name: Nightshare
header.description: Every player owns an equal share of the night. Sleeping spends yours and fast-forwards the night by that slice - cumulative, and nobody has to sleep at the same time.

settings.text: §lNightshare§r - every player online at nightfall owns an equal share of the night. Getting into bed spends yours and fast-forwards the night by that slice. Shares add up over the night, and nobody has to sleep at the same time.
§7Changes here take effect the next time the world loads.§r

options.name: auto
options.text: Hold it back while someone is away

settings.text: §7Minecraft ends the night by itself once everyone in the Overworld is asleep. Players in the Nether or End cannot sleep at all, so that really means §oeveryone who could sleep did§r§7.§r
§7§lLet it happen§r§7 accepts that. If a friend is off in the Nether and the rest of you turn in, morning comes even though their share was never spent.§r

§7§lHold it back while someone is away§r§7 makes the night run exactly as long as the unspent shares say. The cost: while somebody is away, anyone getting into bed sees Minecraft claim night skipping is switched off. It is not - Nightshare is holding it.§r
§7§lAlways hold it back§r§7 shows that same message every time anyone sleeps, on every night.§r

§7How long the sky takes to sweep forward when a share is spent. Every skip takes this long whatever its size, so one player skipping a whole night and one of ten skipping a tenth feel the same. Raise it if the sky looks jumpy.§r
§7Post a line when someone turns in, showing how much of the night they gave and how many shares are in so far.§r
